Caustic

KAW-stik -- the first syllable rhymes with 'saw'. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Caustic is sarcastic in a bitter, biting way.

The comedian's caustic jokes about the town's losing streak drew laughter from some neighbors and winces from others.

Worked Example

After the nervous singer finishes her first recital, her older cousin smirks and says, 'Well, at least the piano was in tune.'

That remark is caustic: it wears the disguise of a compliment but is really a bitter, mocking put-down designed to sting. Caustic humor does not just tease -- it burns.

How Caustic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

scathing

scathing: harshly and hurtfully critical

biting

biting: sharp and wounding in tone

sardonic

sardonic: mocking in a scornful, cynical way

Antonyms

gentle

gentle: mild and kind in manner

soothing

soothing: calming and comforting

How Strong Is It? — biting → scathing → caustic

biting vs. caustic

biting vs. caustic: Biting is sharp but a shade lighter than caustic -- a biting comment nips and stings, while a caustic one is soaked in bitterness and leaves a mark that lasts.

scathing vs. caustic

scathing vs. caustic: Scathing turns the burn up even past caustic: a caustic remark wounds with bitter sarcasm, while a scathing review or rebuke sets out to scorch its target completely.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — caust-

root — caust-: to burn (Greek kaustikos, from kaiein 'to burn')

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: having the characteristics of; like (Greek -ikos, via Latin -icus)

Put it together

Put it together: Caustic combines Greek caust- ('to burn') with -ic ('having the characteristics of'). Something caustic literally has the character of burning -- and a caustic remark burns exactly that way, scorching its target with bitter sarcasm instead of flame.

Use the root in a new word: cauterize

Use the root in a new word: cauterize: Far from any hospital, the expedition medic had to cauterize the wound with a heated blade to stop the bleeding.

Root Check

Word Choice

Caustic almost always describes words and wit: a caustic remark, caustic humor, a caustic review. It is stronger than 'sarcastic' alone -- the sarcasm has real bitterness in it, meant to sting the person it targets.
